children: Yields on U.K. government bonds, or gilts, are at multi-year highs, adding pressure to already stretched public finances, Handelsbanken's senior U.K. economist Daniel Mahoney says in a note. "Current moves in financial markets are clearly set to further erode the government's fiscal headroom at the upcoming budget," he says. Elevated borrowing costs raise the risk of new tax rises at the budget next month, Mahoney says. Nonetheless, if Middle East tensions ease, this could enable gilt yields to fall, he says. Ten-year gilt yields rise 8 basis points to last trade at 5.285%, having hit a 19-year high of 5.294%, LSEG data show. Thirty-year gilt yields rise to 5.921%, their highest since 1998. (miriam.mukuru@wsj.com)
